tools.name: remove_from_watchlist
tools.description: Remove one stock ticker from the authenticated user's StockLens watchlist. Does NOT execute trades and does NOT delete a recorded holding or its transactions — a watchlist item with recorded transactions cannot be removed through this tool. Does NOT accept more than one ticker per call.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_market_summary" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.detail: Description of "get_market_summary" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: discover_stocks · Private data: add_to_watchlist · Public sink: add_to_watchlist · Destructive: add_to_watchlist, discover_stocks, get_market_summary, initiate_analysis, remove_from_watchlist.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: discover_stocks · Private data: add_to_watchlist · Public sink: add_to_watchlist · Destructive: add_to_watchlist, discover_stocks, get_market_summary, initiate_analysis, remove_from_watchlist

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "discover_stocks" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
